title: Isandro and the Typewriter
premise: In the winter of 1918, in the river town of Verenmoor, Mirabel Galloway — a mapmaker's apprentice finishing the atlas her master died for — hides her identity behind a battered typewriter on which she transcribes documents for the occupying commission. When the bridge, the only road out, closes for the season, the town becomes a sealed vessel of grudges, and Mirabel is pulled into its middle when a typed letter she produced is used to condemn an innocent man. To save him she must expose the forgery, which means betraying the only family she has left — her uncle, the commission's clerk — and choosing which of two fugitives gets the last berth on the season's final barge before the armistice is signed, or isn't. In the end she finishes the atlas, sends her uncle across instead of herself, and stays in Verenmoor as the town's mapmaker, having found belonging not by escaping but by being needed.
about_author: Xanthe Nystrom is the pen name of a former archival cartographer who spent a decade restoring water-damaged maps from occupied European towns. She writes historical fiction about people whose quiet work — ink, type, and paper — decides who lives.

chapters.title: The Weight of Blank Paper
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. She catalogs her dead master's unfinished atlas in the cold map room while the town prepares for the bridge closing. She transcribes a requisition on the commission typewriter, careful to be invisible. Emotional beat: quiet grief and the comfort of routine about to be shattered.

chapters.title: Last Cart Across
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. The bridge closes with a chain and a posted order; her uncle Aldous secures his position as commission clerk. A stranger, Tomas Vey, arrives on the wrong side of the river and asks Mirabel to copy a document. Emotional beat: the trap of the sealed town snapping shut.

chapters.title: The Clerk's Niece
chapters.summary: Aldous's POV. He reflects on raising Mirabel after her parents' disappearance, and on the letter he asks her to type — an accusation against Tomas Vey for theft of commission stores. He tells himself it is justice. Emotional beat: rationalized betrayal.

chapters.title: Ink Under the Fingernails
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. She types the accusation, then notices the phrasing isn't her uncle's voice — someone dictated it. Tomas is arrested that evening. Emotional beat: first crack of doubt turning to dread.

chapters.title: The Atlas Her Master Died For
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Flashback woven in: her master was executed for mapping troop movements for the resistance; the atlas is both his legacy and evidence against her if found. She hides the plates beneath the floor. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Tomas in the Cold Cell
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. In the cell he recalls carrying the master's final map across the river, and why he came back — to find the atlas before the commission does. Emotional beat: loyalty to a dead man over his own survival.

chapters.title: A Trial in a Sealed Town
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. The tribunal convenes; the typed letter is the only evidence. Mirabel realizes the typewriter's 'e' is misaligned and her typed letter doesn't match the exhibit — someone retyped it. Emotional beat: hope arriving as a technicality.

chapters.title: What the 'e' Knew
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. She tests the commission typewriter and proves the exhibit was typed elsewhere — on the master's old machine, missing since his arrest. Someone in town has it. Emotional beat: the hunt beginning, and terror of what it implies.

chapters.title: The Printer's Daughter
chapters.summary: New POV: Odile, the printer's daughter. She has the master's typewriter, smuggled to her by her father before his own arrest. She has been forging commission documents to feed hidden fugitives. Emotional beat: guilt and defiance entwined.

chapters.title: Two Fugitives, One Berth
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The last coal barge before the armistice will carry one person out. Two fugitives need it: Tomas, if freed, and Odile's brother, hunted for the forgeries. Emotional beat: an impossible arithmetic of lives.

chapters.title: Uncle Aldous's Ledger
chapters.summary: Aldous's POV. He discovers Mirabel is investigating the forgery and realizes the dictation came from Captain Reiner, who framed Tomas to cover his own thefts. Aldous weighs his career against his niece. Emotional beat: the loyalty-vs-truth theme made personal.

chapters.title: Night Visit to the Cell
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. She bribes her way to Tomas and tells him she can prove the letter forged — but the proof exposes Odile's forgeries and endangers the hidden fugitives. Tomas asks her not to save him at others' cost. Emotional beat: the cost of justice outside the law.

chapters.title: The Map Room Search
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Reiner, suspicious, searches the map room for the atlas. Mirabel watches him come within a hand's width of the hidden plates. Emotional beat: near-annihilation of everything she's protecting.

chapters.title: A Bargain in the Boathouse
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile offers Reiner a trade: the typewriter and silence about his thefts, in exchange for Tomas's release. Reiner pretends to agree. Emotional beat: hope built on a lie.

chapters.title: The Typed Confession
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Reiner produces a new document — a confession signed 'Tomas Vey,' typed on the master's machine to frame Odile too. Mirabel recognizes her own transcription habits copied into it. Emotional beat: violation; her craft weaponized against her.

chapters.title: Which Family Member
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Aldous is implicated in the cover-up; if Mirabel testifies, he is tried with Reiner. The barge leaves at dawn with one berth. Mirabel must choose: send Aldous out to safety, or give the berth to Odile's brother and let her uncle face the tribunal. Emotional beat: the blurb's choice rendered in full.

chapters.title: The Atlas Goes to the Tribunal
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. She finishes her master's final map — the one proving Reiner's thefts and the resistance's innocence — and walks it into the tribunal herself, choosing truth over both loyalty and safety. Emotional beat: the climax's first strike.

chapters.title: Reiner's Fall
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converging. The map, the misaligned 'e,' and Odile's testimony break Reiner before the armistice news arrives mid-hearing. Tomas is freed; Aldous, having turned evidence, is sentenced to transport instead of the gallows. Emotional beat: catharsis with a bill attached.

chapters.title: The Last Berth
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. At the barge, Mirabel gives the berth to Aldous — not as forgiveness, but because the atlas needs a courier to the capital and Odile's brother is needed here, hidden. Aldous weeps. Emotional beat: love expressed as exile.

chapters.title: Armistice
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Bells, mud, strangers embracing in the square. Tomas chooses not to leave on the next barge; he stays to rebuild the bridge and to stand beside Mirabel. Emotional beat: belonging chosen, not inherited.

chapters.title: Finishing the Atlas
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. She inks the final plate — Verenmoor, the bridge, the river drawn accurately for the first time — and signs both her master's name and her own beneath it. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into legacy.

chapters.title: The Town That Stayed
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV, coda. Spring: the bridge reopens, Odile prints the atlas, and Mirabel takes apprentices of her own. She keeps the misaligned typewriter on her desk as a reminder that truth has a signature. Emotional beat: quiet, earned belonging.
